cross_cutting_observations: All 4 invocations were user-initiated with an explicit /total-recall directive - no autonomous AI-initiated invocations in this batch
Pattern: user states uncertainty about prior work ('i thought we did...', 'i have totally lost it', 'is this complete?') then directs AI to use /total-recall
All 4 invocations resulted in successful context recovery with the AI taking meaningful downstream action
FTS5 tokenization: hyphens are word separators in the underlying search engine (seen in batch5-004). The skill had to reformulate 'review-loop' as '"review loop"' - a recurring fragility
Delivery format is consistent across models (opus-4-6 and sonnet-4-6): structured text with '> **Contextify Total Recall**' header, findings, current state, open questions
The '"Optional Next Step"' search pattern (batch5-003) is a learned heuristic that the AI uses to find session-end summaries as proxies for wrap-up status
Two invocations (batch5-001 and batch5-005) were at the very start of a session (lines 7-8), indicating that Total Recall is being used as a session orientation tool for lost/paused work
Cross-worktree search (batch5-003) is the most demanding use case: required 10+ search/context commands and fallback to git and bloon CLIs. Project ID resolution across worktrees was unreliable.
The negative_proof pattern (batch5-004) is distinct: using Total Recall not to find what was done but to confirm whether a specific task had been performed in any session, to avoid duplication
